title: Evaluation of wound healing active principles in the transdermal patch formulated with crude bio wastes and plant extracts against GSK-3 beta - an in silico study.
authors: Subbukutti, Veerabahu; Sailatha, Ethirajulu; Gunasekaran, Sethu; Manibalan, Subramaniyan; Uma Devi, Kumba Janarthanan; Bhuvaneshwari, Koteeswaran; Suvedha, Rajendran
one_liner_zh: 该研究通过分子对接和MD模拟评估透皮贴剂中天然化合物对GSK-3β的抑制，属于蛋白-小分子互作，非蛋白质-DNA互作体系，与本课题无关。
abstract: The wound-healing process is accelerated by inhibiting proteins that decelerate the wound-healing pathway. One of the active proteins involved in enhancing healing at the nuclear level and in gene expression is catenin. Inhibition of Glycogen Synthase Kinase 3beta (GSK3 beta) phosphorylates and degrades catenin via the downstream Wnt signalling pathway, thereby stabilizing catenin. A medicated wound dressing transdermal patch designed with fusion of bio wastes, viz. physiologically clotted fibrin, fish scale collagen, and the ethanolic extract of Mangifera indica (L.) and spider web, was analysed against GSK3beta to enhance healing. In our earlier studies, the compounds present in the transdermal patch were identified using GC-MS analysis; 12 compounds exhibiting the wound healing mechanism were analyzed using PASS software and filtered out. From these 12 compounds, 6 compounds that possessed drug-likeness were screened by SwissADME and vNN-ADMET to dock against GSK3beta in the present work. The PyRx results confirmed the binding of the six ligands to the active site of the target protein. Though the remaining filtered ligands also exhibited inhibitory activity, Molecular dynamics simulation studies were carried out with 100 ns on a complex of 10,12 Tricosadiyonic acid, Nopyl acetate and 2 Methyl 4 Heptanol as they showed binding affinity of -6.2Kcal/mol, -5.7Kcal/mol and -5.1Kcal/mol respectively. The stability of the complex was validated using MD simulation parameters RMSD, RMSF, Rg, and Number of Hydrogen bonds. These results implied that the transdermal patch would be efficient in accelerating the wound healing process through the inactivation of GSK3beta.Communicated by Ramaswamy H. Sarma.
abstract_zh: 伤口愈合过程通过抑制延缓愈合通路的蛋白质而加速。在核水平和基因表达中参与增强愈合的活性蛋白之一是catenin。抑制糖原合成酶激酶3β（GSK3 beta）通过下游Wnt信号通路磷酸化并降解catenin，从而稳定catenin。本研究设计了一种由生物废弃物融合而成的药用伤口敷料透皮贴片，即生理性凝血纤维蛋白、鱼鳞胶原蛋白、芒果（Mangifera indica (L.)）乙醇提取物和蜘蛛网，并针对GSK3beta进行分析以增强愈合。在我们早期的研究中，使用GC-MS分析鉴定了透皮贴片中的化合物；通过PASS软件分析并筛选出12种具有伤口愈合机制的化合物。从这12种化合物中，通过SwissADME和vNN-ADMET筛选出6种具有药物相似性的化合物，用于在本工作中与GSK3beta进行对接。PyRx结果确认了这六种配体与靶蛋白活性位点的结合。尽管其余筛选出的配体也表现出抑制活性，但分子动力学模拟研究在100 ns下对10,12-二十三碳二炔酸、乙酸诺匹酯和2-甲基-4-庚醇的复合物进行，因为它们分别显示出-6.2Kcal/mol、-5.7Kcal/mol和-5.1Kcal/mol的结合亲和力。复合物的稳定性通过MD模拟参数RMSD、RMSF、Rg和氢键数量进行了验证。这些结果表明，透皮贴片通过灭活GSK3beta可有效加速伤口愈合过程。由Ramaswamy H. Sarma通讯。
